cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). Now he takes on a new topic: food sacrificed to idols. And he opens with something they know: we all have knowledge.

cards.question: Paul puts knowledge and love side by side. Which one does he say builds up?

cards.text: Knowledge puffs up, Paul says, and the one who thinks he knows something doesn't yet know as he ought to. I once KNEW I could grab a hot tray with my bare mustache, and friend, I knew it all the way to the smoke.

cards.question: Then Paul turns to the one who loves God. What does he say about that person?

answers.text: That person is known by God
That person is made wise by God
That person is given every answer

cards.text: Okay, BACK to the food. Paul lays out what they know about idols.

cards.question: Paul says an idol is a real power in the world.

cards.text: Paul says there are many so-called gods and lords, in heaven or on earth. SO-CALLED, friend, like the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with, swearing they still had a little charge left.
But for us, Paul says, there's one God, the Father. All things came from Him, and we exist for Him.

cards.question: Paul names one God, the Father. Who does he name as the one Lord?
Paul says all things came through Jesus Christ.

cards.text: Paul's still on the food question, and here comes the catch. Not everyone has this knowledge.

cards.question: Some people are still so used to idols. How do they eat this food?

answers.text: As if it were sacrificed to an idol
As if it were nothing at all
As if it were a holy offering

cards.question: Paul says the people still used to idols have a strong conscience.

cards.text: Their conscience is weak, Paul says, so it's defiled. Then he turns to the food itself, and whether it changes anything between us and God.

cards.question: Paul says eating food sacrificed to idols brings a person closer to God.

cards.text: Eat it or skip it, Paul says, you're no worse and no better. And I'm telling you this as a stamper who lives on a COOKIE PLANET: food does not get you closer to God.
So the well-informed ones have freedom here, and after years in a junk drawer, believe me, I LOVE freedom. But Paul says be careful.

cards.question: Paul warns the well-informed believers that their freedom could become a stumbling block to the weak.

cards.text: Then Paul paints the picture. Someone with a weak conscience sees you, the well-informed one, eating in an idol's temple.

cards.question: Paul says seeing a well-informed believer eat in an idol's temple would encourage someone with a weak conscience to stay away from food sacrificed to idols.

cards.text: Here's where it gets heavy. Paul calls him the weak brother, for whom Christ died, and says wounding a weak conscience like his is sinning against your brothers.

cards.question: Paul says something destroys that weak brother. What is it?

answers.text: The priests who serve the idol

cards.question: Sinning against your brothers by wounding their weak conscience, Paul says, is sinning against ___.

cards.text: Then Paul makes it personal. He stops saying what YOU should do and starts saying what HE will do.

cards.question: Paul says if what he eats causes his brother to stumble, what will he do?

cards.text: Keep your apron on, friend. Paul's teaching isn't done yet.
